summary: Today’s pulse tracks Clive Davis, music mogul behind Whitney Houston and Bruce Springsteen, dies aged 94, Did you know? Alan Greenspan and Ayn Rand were close friends, and Rail passengers told to only travel if essential amid red extreme heat warning. Across BBC, NPR, and Guardian, the strongest repeated signals are starmer, minister, and prime. In the background, Andy Burnham sworn in as an MP after Keir Starmer resigns as prime minister - UK politics live and Two Britons plead guilty to £39m 2024 cyber-attack on Transport for London keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: Did you know? Alan Greenspan and Ayn Rand were close friends
headlines.description: One of the most intellectually important relationships in the life of the late Fed chair Alan Greenspan was with his close friend, the formidable novelist and libertarian thinker Ayn Rand.

headlines.title: Rail passengers told to only travel if essential amid red extreme heat warning
headlines.description: Network Rail expected impose speed restrictions, with people told to check if train services are running Rail passengers have been told to only attempt to travel if essential and check trains are running, with extreme heat expected to disrupt services around Britain. Temperatures are forecast to rise to 37C across most of southern England and Wales over the next three days, and potentially to 40C in the most affected areas.

headlines.title: Andy Burnham sworn in as an MP after Keir Starmer resigns as prime minister - UK politics live
headlines.description: The prime minister said a new leader will be in place before parliament returns in September Full report: Keir Starmer to step down as prime minister two years after historic election victory Wes Streeting backs Andy Burnham to become Labour leader and PM Keir Starmer’s time as prime minister – in pictures This is from Tom Baldwin , Keir Starmer’s biographer, and head of communications for Ed Miliband when he was Labour leader. We seem to be in a strange place where Keir Starmer is being told he must quit to prevent more uncertainty and chaos (by those who have caused much of it) but then stay on for a couple of months because the guy who has been desperate to take his job is not yet ready to do so… Keir Starmer has a mandate from Labour members. He stood on a manifesto and won a mandate from the British people Modern politics: Consumerisation

headlines.title: Two Britons plead guilty to £39m 2024 cyber-attack on Transport for London
headlines.description: Thalha Jubair and Owen Flowers, linked to the Scattered Spider hacking group, change pleas on first day of trial Two British cybercriminals from the Scattered Spider hacking group have pleaded guilty to a cyber-attack on Transport for London in 2024 that cost £39m and affected 10 million people. Thalha Jubair, 20, and Owen Flowers, 18, pleaded guilty to offences under the Computer Misuse Act at Woolwich crown court on Monday.

headlinePool.title: Iran agrees to UN nuclear inspectors’ return as part of agreement with US
headlinePool.description: Other measures include Washington lifting sanctions on Tehran’s oil exports and reopening the strait of Hormuz Middle East crisis live – latest updates Iran has agreed to allow UN nuclear inspectors back into the country as part of an agreement under which Washington will lift sanctions on Tehran’s oil exports and the strait of Hormuz will reopen, the US vice-president, JD Vance, has said. Long-term independent monitoring of Iran’s nuclear programme, which it says is for energy purposes only, was in effect halted last summer after Israel and the US attacked the country. Tehran suspended cooperation with the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) in response to strikes on its nuclear facilities.

headlinePool.title: US supreme court reinstates murder conviction in case of Etan Patz
headlinePool.description: Appeals court had ruled Pedro Hernandez, 64, was wrongly convicted over 1979 disappearance of New York six-year-old The US supreme court has reinstated a murder conviction in the long winding case of Etan Patz , whose 1979 disappearance at age six from New York City garnered national headlines. In a 6-3 decision on Monday, the supreme court agreed with New York prosecutors in their request to reverse a lower court ruling that had thrown out the murder conviction of Pedro Hernandez, 64, in the Patz case.

headlinePool.title: ‘Institutional threat’: election of far-right leader raises fears for democracy in Colombia
headlinePool.description: Trump-admiring Abelardo de la Espriella has vowed to ‘disembowel’ the left and kill criminals like ‘rats and cockroaches’ When more than 20 women accused a Colombian evangelical pastor in 2012 of sexually abusing them, the defendant’s lawyer sought to discredit the allegations by telling the court that they were “ trepadoras ” – a pejorative term meaning social climbers. He ultimately secured his client’s acquittal – although the case remains under review by the supreme court – but footage of the remark resurfaced during Colombia’s presidential campaign, sparking outrage among many progressive voters.

headlinePool.title: Jeffrey Donaldson found guilty of child sexual offences including rape
headlinePool.description: Former DUP leader convicted of 18 offences against two victims after high-profile trial that gripped Northern Ireland ‘A sinful nature’: how Jeffrey Donaldson was unmasked as a sexual predator Jeffrey Donaldson has been found guilty of 18 sexual offences against two victims who were children at the time of the abuse more than 30 years ago. The former Democratic Unionist party (DUP) leader was remanded into immediate custody after a jury at Newry crown court on Monday convicted him of 18 offences including rape, indecent assault and gross indecency. The judge, Paul Ramsey, said a “lengthy” prison sentence was inevitable.

headlinePool.title: Trump claims ‘vandals’ foiled his $14m bid to revamp DC’s reflecting pool. What actually happened?
headlinePool.description: Trump’s pre-Fourth of July renovation project has endured problems with algae, peeling paint and an inflating price tag Donald Trump’s rush to repaint the Lincoln Memorial reflecting pool, an iconic symbol of Washington DC, has hit roadblock after roadblock as the country’s 250th anniversary nears. The public has been gripped by the ill-fated $14m bid to renovate the reflecting pool, which the US president vowed to make “beautiful” in time for this summer’s birthday celebrations at the capital.
